title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Remove everything unused, in one go
summary: One command instead of five, repeating until a pass finds nothing, because each removal orphans the next.

highlights.title: Remove Everything Unused
highlights.description: Five commands removed five kinds of dead code, and one pass was never enough: on a real project the removals only settled after four rounds. This asks once, then does all of it, repeating until a pass finds nothing.

sections.heading: Added
bullets: Remove Everything Unused: declarations, class members, enum entries, dead islands, locals and parameters, plus the imports and files they orphan, in one command that repeats until a pass finds nothing.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: The per file sweep carried its own copy of the removal extent, left behind while the original grew. A multi line initializer had no removal there while the same shape had one elsewhere.
The watcher added in 1.42.243 had no exclusion filter, so the thousands of files a build writes under `build/` emptied the corpus cache over and over.
